subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw support headless persistent child sessions for `sessions_spawn(mode="session")` without channel thread binding, and should that contract apply to both native subagents and ACP runtime spawns?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the requested fix changes durable session lifecycle, routing, cleanup, and channel delivery semantics rather than only repairing a narrow regression.

options.title: Define headless persistent sessions
options.body: Specify non-thread `mode="session"` semantics for both ACP and native subagents, then implement with focused tests for `sessions_send`, cleanup, and delivery behavior.

options.title: Keep session mode thread-bound
options.body: Leave runtime behavior intact and improve docs/tool copy around `mode="run"`, `sessions_send`, and supported thread-bound channels.

options.title: Limit to ACP affinity only
options.body: Add a separate ACP persistence contract such as affinity-backed sessions while keeping native `mode="session"` thread-bound.

recommendation.title: Define headless persistent sessions
recommendation.body: Specify non-thread `mode="session"` semantics for both ACP and native subagents, then implement with focused tests for `sessions_send`, cleanup, and delivery behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The ACP thread-bound session implementation is the most product-sensitive half of the requested behavior, and this owner introduced that runtime surface.
